title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache cost model (Horizon Finance)
meeting_header: Date: 2027-01-18 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Liu (Redwood SE), Daniel Green (CTO, Horizon), Maya Torres (Platform Eng), Leo Park (SRE)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Horizon Finance through Redwood Optimize recommendations focusing on batching and prefix/KV cache usage. Discussed tradeoffs between latency and token cost, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), and a cost model tailored to Horizon's 50 qps conversational workload. Action: Samir to share cost spreadsheet and config examples; Horizon to provision sample traces for benchmarking.
next_steps: Samir to send cost and config spreadsheet (includes batching sims) by 2027-01-20
Horizon to upload 24h trace sample to shared s3 link by 2027-01-25
Schedule benchmark run with Horizon infra week of 2027-01-25
Follow-up demo showing canary rollout and autoscale config w/ Maya
action_items: Samir Patel: send cost model spreadsheet and example batch configs - due 2027-01-20
Maya Torres: share 24h request trace and sample prompts - due 2027-01-25
Jia Liu: prepare benchmark run plan and instance sizing recommendation - due 2027-01-22
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick 60 minute walkthrough of Optimize focusing on batching and the KV prefix cache and then leave time for q&a
[00:12] Daniel (Customer/CTO): thanks, Samir, excited — we've been digging into token costs, our spend for the last quarter jumped, so hoping to see concrete levers.
[00:20] Jia (SE): cool, quick intro from me, Jia Liu, I work on inference performance and cost ops at Redwood, I'll show the cost model spreadsheet and live sims. Apologies if audio is a bit fuzzy, our rdp connection is on and off.
[00:35] Maya: no worries, we're remote today, same here.
[00:40] Samir: quick agenda, 1) batching fundamentals and cont batching, 2) prefix vs KV cache use cases, 3) cost model for Horizon's workload, 4) recommended config and next steps.
[01:02] Jia: ok starting with batching, uh so continuous batching groups requests and we balance latency SLOs with throughput. for Horizon at 50 qps with average 60 token responses we saw in your trace, there's room to batch 8-12 requests on peak while staying under 150ms p50 if you tune max_wait. note there are transcription quips here — some numbers rounded.
[01:29] Leo (SRE): sorry can you restate p50 numbers? our SLA is 120ms p50 for token streaming endpoints.
[01:36] Jia: yep, for streaming generation p50 120ms is tight but achievable if you reduce max_batch_wait to 10-12ms and target batch sizes of 6-8. larger batches reduce cost per token but increase tail latency.
[01:50] Samir: important callout — batching helps token cost linearly but impacts cold-start and long-tail latency. so tradeoff.
[02:03] Daniel: what's the delta in cost if we go from no batching to an average batch of 8?
[02:10] Jia: in our model that Horizon spreadsheet I'll share, cost/token drops about 28-35% depending on model quantization and GPU type. we assumed a 16-bit model on A100-like hardware for hosted, and q4_0 quant for dedicated gives extra 10-12% savings.
[02:32] Maya: and kv cache — how does that interact with batching? we've got a lot of repeated prompts for account lookups.
[02:40] Jia: great Q. prefix cache is good for repeated initial prompts across sessions, KV cache is per-conversation kv cache of decoder keys. for Horizon use case, we recommend hybrid: prefix cache for common system prompts/templates and KV cache for conversation continuity. KV cache reduces compute on long histories by reusing past keys; batching still applies for the next-token steps but with smaller compute since kv is warm.
[03:05] Leo: what about memory — KV cache can blow up on GPU memory, any guidance?
[03:12] Jia: yes, memory is the big constraint. we modelled a 6M token/day active cache size for you and that maps to roughly 40-60GB of KV depending on sequence length and model layer count. our Dedicated plan lets you pin nodes with extra vram and we support selective eviction policies.
[03:32] Samir: also note you can tier cache — keep hot keys in GPU, warm keys in fast NVMe, cold on disk. Redwood Optimize suggests eviction TTLs based on recency and hit rate.
[03:45] Daniel: security — does cache persist in cleartext? our compliance team will ask about encryption at rest.
[03:52] Jia: good — KV cache in hosted is encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with your HSM. audit logs show cache access and eviction events in Console.
[04:10] Maya: do you have SOC2 docs?
[04:14] Samir: yes, we'll attach SOC2 Type II and our security whitepaper in the follow up.
[04:20] Jia: back to cost model, here's the simplified equation we use: total_cost = (compute_cost_per_second * total_runtime_seconds) + storage_and_network. but practically we model tokens served, cache hit rate, batch size, and GPU hourly price.
[04:38] Daniel: can you show a couple of example scenarios?
[04:42] Jia: sure — scenario A: hosted, no batching, no cache: baseline cost X; scenario B: batching avg 8, prefix cache 30% hit, KV warm 20% hit: cost drops to ~0.56X. scenario C: dedicated with q4_0 quant and optimized batching + cache: ~0.42X. these are illustrative; I'll send the spreadsheet with the exact numbers for your traces.
[05:08] Leo: do these assume fixed token lengths? our user messages vary a lot, some 20 tokens, some 400.
[05:15] Jia: yeah we use a distribution from your sample traces — median 60, 90th 210 tokens. batching benefit is best when response sizes are similar; variable lengths reduce packing efficiency. we also model padding overhead.
[05:33] Samir: quick interjection — for variance we recommend adaptive batching policies: set max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, and per-route hints to avoid long tail. we can recommend defaults for your routes.
[05:48] Daniel: curious about fallback behavior — if dedicated pool is saturated, do requests go to hosted automatically?
[05:54] Jia: yes, smart routing can failover to hosted model variant with a slightly higher latency or lower throughput guarantee. you control routing policy in Console with priority and cost thresholds.
[06:10] Maya: can we pin model ver to an earlier release for stability?
[06:14] Samir: yep, Console supports model pinning and can manage rollouts (canary, A/B) and automatic fallback. we'll demo that in follow up.
[06:25] Daniel: network egress — we have data residency rules, can we keep everything in our VPC?
[06:31] Jia: for Private deployments we can run control plane in your VPC and keep infer nodes in your network; you also get KMS integration and audit events streamed to your SIEM. for Dedicated we offer private networking options too.
[06:44] Leo: ok show us the spreadsheet and the sim.
[06:48] Jia: launching screen share now, sorry some graphical glitch, but here's the cost sheet. columns: route, qps, avg_resp_tokens, batch_policy, cache_hit_rate, compute_cost, net_cost. row for Horizon's "account-summary" route shows qps 12 peak, avg 48 tokens, predicted savings 33% with our recommended settings.
[07:15] Samir: note the sensitivity tab — we ran MC sims for hit rate from 10-70% and batch sizes 1-16. for your workload the sweet spot was batch 6-8 with KV hit 18-25% depending on session reuse.
[07:33] Maya: what's effort to implement? we have a small infra team, want clear steps and telemetry.
[07:40] Samir: low to medium. steps: 1) instrument request sampling to produce a 24h trace, 2) upload to Redwood shared bucket, 3) we run sim and provide batch policy + recommended node types, 4) you can apply batch hints via SDK or route config, 5) run pilot on Dedicated with limited workload. Jia will run benchmarks with you.
[08:05] Jia: and Console gives per-route token breakdown, batch histograms and cache hit dashboards so you can iteratively tune.
[08:15] Daniel: any risk to correctness? will caching affect model outputs, e.g., if we reuse prefix cache incorrectly?
[08:22] Jia: prefix cache is safe for static system prompts and template text; KV cache preserves state of past tokens — correctness preserved. but you should validate with eval prompts: Redwood Optimize ties into your evals so we can check regression.
[08:37] Leo: what's the expected timescale to see savings?
[08:40] Samir: depends but typically within 2-4 weeks of pilot: instrumentation -> pilot -> tune.
[08:46] Maya: ok, legal will want indemnity language for our PII usage, and encryption details.
[08:52] Samir: we'll include security pack and standard DPA language in the follow up.
[08:58] Daniel: great. last Q — do you support cold start mitigation for bursty traffic?
[09:03] Jia: yes, we recommend a small warm pool and autoscale policy with burst buffer. it reduces cost slightly but avoids long cold tail.
[09:12] Samir: ok wrapping — recap, we will send the spreadsheet and sample batch configs, Horizon to share traces, Jia to prep benchmark plan, schedule run around Jan 25. any final?
[09:25] Maya: nope, thanks all.
[09:28] Daniel: thanks, Samir, Jia.
[09:30] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and docs. bye.
notes_on_quality: Transcript has minor transcription errors and occasional speaker mislabels (common with call recording). Technical terms like q4_0 quant, KV cache, and cont batching are sometimes slightly garbled.
